title: The same legacy player behind an object adapter and a class adapter

blocks.text: The page's Q2 adapts one legacy player to the `MediaPlayer` interface in two ways:

items: an **object adapter** holds a `LegacyAudioPlayer` and **delegates to the player it was given**, so it works with any subclass of it;
a **class adapter** `extends LegacyAudioPlayer implements MediaPlayer` and **calls the method it inherits**.

blocks.text: Neither adds behaviour: **the call passes through unchanged**, and whatever the legacy player throws reaches the caller.
Given: `MediaPlayer` and `LegacyAudioPlayer` (its `playMp3` refuses a blank name with `IllegalArgumentException`). Write both adapters:

items: `new AudioPlayerAdapter(player)`: **`null` is refused at once** with `NullPointerException`; `getPlayerType()` is `"Audio (Object Adapter)"`.

cases.says: Both adapters answer play("song.mp3") with the legacy player's "Playing MP3: song.mp3" and report their own player type.
Given a subclass of LegacyAudioPlayer that overrides playMp3, the object adapter returns what that subclass returns.
A subclass of AudioClassAdapter that overrides playMp3 changes what play returns, because the class adapter calls its own inherited method.
The adapters pass the filename on untouched: " song.mp3" keeps its space, and a blank name reaches the legacy player, which throws IllegalArgumentException.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A class adapter extends the adaptee and implements the target, calling the methods it inherits, so single inheritance limits it to one adaptee class.
An adapter validates its adaptee eagerly with Objects.requireNonNull, so a null fails at construction rather than on a later call.
An object adapter implements the target interface and delegates to the adaptee it holds, so it works with any subclass of that adaptee.
An adapter only translates the interface and adds no behaviour, so calls and the adaptee's exceptions pass through unchanged.
